name: Detail an Object
about: The detailed version of an Object, for renders only (it is never placed in the model): built in Blender from the brief and its photos, to the instancing standard, on a PC. A Project Object's detail is kept in its project; a Library Object's is proposed to the Library. The files stay on this PC.
useWhen: The owner wants an Object's full model for renders: a Project Object (in a project) or a Library Object (from the Library), matching the real product in its photos.

input.about: In a project: the Project Object to detail (params.object) and its photos from the project's files. From the Library: the Library Object is the run's subject. Anything to know in the notes.

rules.text: Real-world scale; one master mesh per repeated part and linked duplicates for the repeats; the instance audit passes.
The model matches the real product in the photos: proportions, joints, thicknesses, finishes and colours; where the photo and the brief differ, the brief wins and the difference is said.
The .blend stays on the PC that built it, by its Helper's named folder and path; the .usdc, .glb and the preview come to the run.

The detail is the Object's third form, for renders only: it is never placed in the model. Only the owner's decision keeps it: beside the Project Object in its project, or proposed beside the Library Object (a pull request the owner merges).

steps.name: Build
steps.outcome: The Object is built as a detailed model: its .blend kept on the PC, its .usdc, .glb, a preview and a passing audit sent to the run.

steps.name: Keep the detail
steps.question: Does the preview match the photos? Keep the files as the Object's detail, or send it back with what to change.

output.name: Detail
output.about: The detailed files kept, and the Object's new version that points to them.
